docs.title: Installing nyxd on Linux
docs.description: nyxd runs on any Linux host that meets the kernel and tooling requirements below (desktop, VM, VPS, edge box, ARM or x86). It was first written for a home Raspberry Pi so containers could run without Docker or a heavy daemon; that same footprint applies everywhere you want a minimal stack.

docs.title: QEMU + Alpine 3.23 for nyxd hacking
docs.description: Use a small Alpine Linux 3.23 VM when you want to try nyxd on your laptop (x86_64) or exercise aarch64 under QEMU before deploying to bare metal or an ARM board (e.g. a Raspberry Pi).

docs.title: Overview
docs.description: nyxd is a minimal OCI container orchestrator for Linux, built around crun and a small control plane.

docs.title: Benchmarks: nyxd vs Docker vs Podman (Alpine 3.23 / QEMU)
docs.description: Compare the same workload on three as similar as possible Alpine Linux 3.23 guests under QEMU. One VM runs Docker, one Podman, one nyxd + nyx. Goal: apples-to-apples numbers for startup, resource use, and steady-state behavior—not a claim of “fastest in all cases.”
